close_reason: Resolved by replacing the doc-only deprecation with permanent-legacy-alias framing. Type-level #[deprecated] is impossible (Rust can't deprecate a single discriminator value of an enum variant), and removing the alias at any future major bump would silently break backends still emitting TooManyChanges{limit:0} — their returns would stop mapping to cannotCalculateChanges and start producing a malformed RFC 8620 §5.6 tooManyChanges{limit:0}. The honest contract is 'preserved permanently'. Updated jmap-server backend.rs (variant doc, type doc, Display impl comment, From impl comment, limit field doc, two test docs) plus the two sibling-crate copies of the same language (jmap-metadata-server/memory.rs, jmap-sharing-server/principal.rs). Match arms in extensions SHOULD treat TooManyChanges{limit:0} and CannotCalculate as a single 'full-resync required' case. Commit 7fef1d2.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:610 says:

> **Deprecated sub-case (bd:JMAP-jfia.31)**: a `limit` of `0`
> historically meant 'full state reset required' and is
> preserved as an alias for the new [`Self::CannotCalculate`]
> variant. New code SHOULD use `CannotCalculate` directly; the
> alias may be removed at the next major-version bump.

The documentation promises a deprecation path. But:

1. The `TooManyChanges` variant itself cannot be marked #[deprecated] — that would also deprecate non-zero `limit` values, which are the canonical path.

2. The magic-zero sub-case cannot be marked #[deprecated] at the type level because enum-variant pattern shapes don't support discriminator-conditional deprecation in Rust.

3. There is NO runtime warning, NO clippy lint, NO log emission when a backend returns TooManyChanges { limit: 0 }. The only signal to a downstream consumer is the docstring — which they may never read.

4. The 'may be removed at the next major-version bump' commitment in the doc is incompatible with the workspace's actual versioning posture. The crate is pre-1.0; major bumps are cheap. But every *-server extension that pattern-matches on TooManyChanges (e.g. for logging, for retry decisions) must include the magic-zero discriminator or its match becomes wrong:

     match e {
         BackendChangesError::TooManyChanges { limit } if limit > 0 => /* retry path */,
         BackendChangesError::TooManyChanges { limit: 0 } => /* full-resync path */,
         BackendChangesError::CannotCalculate => /* full-resync path */,
         ...
     }

   That's the burden — every consumer carries two arms for one logical case.

5. When the variant is removed at the major bump, callers that ONLY emitted CannotCalculate are forward-compatible. But callers using the canonical 'sometimes I emit zero to mean cannotCalculate' shape (kith and stoa both predate this refactor) will silently change behaviour. Their TooManyChanges { limit: 0 } returns will become well-typed but stop mapping to cannotCalculateChanges — they'll map to tooManyChanges with limit 0 on the wire, which is a malformed RFC 8620 §5.6 response.

Mitigations the doc could promise but doesn't:

(a) Add a `legacy_cannot_calculate()` constructor on BackendChangesError that returns CannotCalculate but is marked #[deprecated] — gives migration callers a deprecation warning at the construction site rather than at the match site.

(b) Add a #[doc(hidden)] feature flag `legacy-cannot-calculate-zero` that, when off, converts the magic-zero alias into a hard error at the From impl (production should run with this off; only the existing-consumer migration window should turn it on).

(c) Add a compile-time helper `BackendChangesError::cannot_calculate()` that wraps the canonical variant; document that any code constructing `TooManyChanges { limit: 0 }` directly is using the legacy shape.

The current shape: 'doc says deprecated, but every match arm in every extension still has to support it' is the worst of both worlds.

Filed P2 under api-contract,versioning because the deprecation path is doc-only and the wire-format risk on removal is real.
title: BackendChangesError::TooManyChanges { limit: 0 } documented as deprecated alias but not marked #[deprecated]
